Concerns were raised by a third party regarding the distribution of women with liver cirrhosis between Tables\u00a01 and 3 in the study, as they and the Child\u2010Pugh scores all differ between these tables when the numbers should remain the same. The publisher asked the authors to clarify these inconsistencies and provide the raw data for the study. The authors did not provide the requested data but responded to the concerns. Upon review of their response, the editorial team and publisher did not feel it explained these serious concerns adequately. Subsequently, further concerns were identified, including irreproducible odds ratios, lack of a reference category, and contradictions between the confidence intervals and p\u2010values in the tables. In addition, the journal sought a clinical opinion from an expert in the area who felt that some of the clinical findings and outcome were not consistent with the typical clinical course of the condition. As a result, the data and conclusions are considered unreliable, and therefore the article must be retracted.\n
